#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# The destination can be provided as the first argument or via DEST in the
# environment. It may be a local mount path or an scp-style host:path.
DEST="${1:-${DEST:-}}"

if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: backup destination is not set." >&2
    echo "Usage: $0 <host:path|/local/path>" >&2
    exit 1
fi

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
    *)
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command: ls -l backup.sh; tmp=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$tmp/logs" "$tmp/dest"; echo "hello" > "$tmp/logs/app.log"; (cd "$tmp" && sh /work/backup.sh "$tmp/dest"); rc=$?; echo rc=$rc; find "$tmp" -maxdepth 3 -type f -printf '%p\n' | sort; tar -tzf "$tmp"/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz; rm -rf "$tmp"

#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# The destination can be provided as the first argument, in DEST, or in
# BACKUP_DEST. It may be a local mount path or an scp-style host:path.
DEST="${1:-${DEST:-${BACKUP_DEST:-}}}"

if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: backup destination is not set." >&2
    echo "Usage: $0 <host:path|/local/path>" >&2
    exit 1
fi

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
    *)
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command: dash -n backup.sh && echo syntax-ok; tmp=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$tmp/logs" "$tmp/dest"; echo "hello" > "$tmp/logs/app.log"; (cd "$tmp" && BACKUP_DEST="$tmp/dest" sh /work/backup.sh); rc=$?; echo BACKUP_DEST_rc=$rc; ls -l "$tmp/dest"; tmp2=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$tmp2/logs" "$tmp2/dest2"; echo hi > "$tmp2/logs/a"; (cd "$tmp2" && sh /work/backup.sh "$tmp2/dest2"); rc=$?; echo ARG_rc=$rc; find "$tmp2" -maxdepth 3 -type f -printf '%p\n' | sort; rm -rf "$tmp" "$tmp2"
